title: Custom SQL Pools for Fabric Data Warehouse (workload governance)
summary: Custom SQL Pools cap the maximum share of warehouse compute a workload can consume (application-name, regex, or SQL statement-type classification), for workload ISOLATION and predictable resource usage — NOT a spending limit. Read the config with 'warehouse get-sql-pools-config' and apply one with 'warehouse update-sql-pools-config'. Good candidates: ETL/data-loading, background processing, and Power BI reporting that must not starve other workloads. Under allocation-based billing, capping a bursty workload's peak allocation can indirectly reduce consumption (it runs longer at a lower vNode peak).
what_it_is: A governance boundary that limits the maximum percentage of warehouse resources a classified workload can access. Its primary purpose is workload isolation (keep a business-critical Power BI dashboard from contending with an aggressive ETL job); with allocation-based billing, governing allocation also affects consumption.
what_it_is_not: NOT a spending limit, monthly budget cap, or '$X/month maximum' — it does not stop charges after a threshold.
NOT a performance boost — it TRADES performance for a smaller/steadier resource footprint (a capped query may run longer at a lower peak).
good_candidates: ETL / data loading that cares about completion, not finishing a few minutes faster.
Power BI reporting you want to guarantee a fixed share so it cannot consume the whole warehouse during business hours.
Bursty workloads that frequently trigger the one-minute minimum allocation window — capping the scale peak can lower billed vNode-seconds.

config_shape.note: The endpoint (PATCH/GET /workspaces/{ws}/warehouses/sqlPoolsConfiguration) is workspace-scoped (governs all warehouses in the workspace). It no longer requires the former beta=true query parameter. Classifier type accepts Application Name, Application Name Regex, or Statement Type.
config_shape.toggle: customSQLPoolsEnabled (bool) turns the feature on/off; customSQLPools is the array of pool definitions.

recommended_workflow: 1. Configure the pools ONCE in the Fabric Portal (Workspace settings) to produce a valid, classifier-correct configuration.
2. Capture the raw configuration without fabio's JSON data envelope: fabio warehouse get-sql-pools-config --workspace $WS -o plain > pools.json
3. Version pools.json in git and re-apply it to other workspaces/environments: fabio warehouse update-sql-pools-config --workspace $WS2 --file pools.json (use --dry-run first).
This 'portal once, then GET → version → update' pattern avoids fabricating the pool schema while making the configuration reproducible and auditable.
gotchas: The config is WORKSPACE-scoped (sqlPoolsConfiguration lives under /warehouses/, not a single warehouse id) — it governs all warehouses in the workspace.
The former required ?beta=true query parameter was removed when this API graduated from beta.
Classifier type is case-sensitive and accepts `Application Name`, `Application Name Regex`, or `Statement Type`; Statement Type values are SQL statement names such as `SELECT`.
Reading and updating SQL pools configuration require workspace Admin.

PATCH customSQLPools replaces the pool list: pools omitted from the request are deleted. Capture the baseline, confirm the workspace, and retain every pool you want to keep. Use -o plain when saving the GET response for --file; default JSON output has a data envelope and is not itself a valid PATCH body.

Each pool needs an explicit isDefault boolean in PATCH requests even though the swagger does not mark it required. Use singular classifier: {type:'Statement Type',value:['SELECT']} (not classifiers[] or a scalar value). A successful GET adds optimizeForReads:true when it was omitted.
Looking ahead (per Microsoft): identity-based classifiers and configurable built-in SELECT/NONSELECT workload groups are planned — future config shapes may add those.
see_also: Configure Custom SQL Pools in the Fabric Portal (Microsoft Learn)
